page: OVHcloud c3-4 is a compute-optimized virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 2 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs from the AMD EPYC processor family running at 2.3 GHz, with 2 physical cores and 1 thread per core. The hardware configuration includes 4.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core, and is bundled with 50 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The instance also includes one complimentary public IPv4 address and has a baseline network bandwidth of 0 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-core performance, with the stress-ng single-core CPU test scoring 3083.56 and the Geekbench single-core test reaching 1920.0, both placing in the top 25% of tested servers. Geekbench text processing also shows strong results at 2412.0. However, multi-core and memory-bound performance is significantly more limited. The Geekbench multi-core score of 3460.0 and the Passmark CPU score of 5442.44 fall into the bottom 25%, reflecting the physical core count limitation. Memory performance is also constrained, with a Passmark memory score of 1378.22 and a weak cached small-block read-only memory bandwidth of 294.72 GB/sec.

The primary tradeoff of the c3-4 instance is its low memory-to-CPU ratio of 2 GB per core and its weak multi-threaded scaling, as evidenced by a weak multi-threaded bzip3 decompression speed of 26.9 GB/sec and poor static web serving throughput of 2.57 GB/sec. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated AMD EPYC cores offer reliable, non-shared compute resources for workloads that require predictable single-thread execution without the overhead of shared-core environments, though it is less suited for memory-intensive or highly parallelized operations.

Given these performance characteristics, the OVHcloud c3-4 is best suited for single-threaded applications, lightweight text processing, simple utility scripts, and basic compute tasks that benefit from dedicated CPU allocation but do not demand high memory capacity or high-throughput web serving. It is not recommended for database operations, heavy multi-threaded compilation, or high-traffic web hosting.
